To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the permeability of the rat blood–brain barrier (BBB) to l-noradrenalines is reduced by jaundice.

The permeability of blood–brain barrier (BBB) to noradrenalaine is not increased in rats with experimental biliary obstruction, but that noradrenaline uptake is inhibited in brain homogenates in the presence of jaundice plasma.

“The blood–brain barrier in jaundice is not impaired, noradrenaline uptake by brain homogenate is inhibited by jaundiced plasma, and the inhibition is not due to a change in the activity of COMT or MAO.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the permeability of the rat blood–brain barrier for noradrenaline in jaundiced rats.
the effects of jaundice and its treatment on the cerebral metabolism of noradrenalines.
the effects of the presence of jaundice in the blood on the uptake of noradrenalines into the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
jaundice is not associated with a general impairment of the blood– brain barrier to noradrenergic substances.
the uptake of noradrenalene into rat brain is inhibited by jaundiced plasma.
the cerebral uptake of noradrenalne in jaundice was not enhanced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
jaundice does not cause any change in the permeability of the brain barrier to noradrenaine, and the reduced cerebral uptake of noradrenalaine is caused by an inhibitory factor in the plasma.

jaundiced plasma contains an inhibitor of noradrenalinespecific transport at the blood–brain interface, which may be responsible for the impairment of cerebral function observed in jaundiced patients.

the brain uptake of noradrenalaine is not increased in jaudiced rats.
